newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha rallies with crude, wet market dry.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha rallies with crude, wet market dry.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices rose modestly on the back of higher crude oil futures but the cargo market was quiet with no deals heard done yet.
June swaps edged up $1.50 to $182.50/$184 a tonne and kept its backwardation at about $3 to July, which traded at $179.50/$180.50. August was valued at $179/$180.
NWE cargoes were notionally valued at $183/$185 cif, unchanged from Thursday.
Traders and brokers maintained that end-user demand was lacklustre and supplies balanced, even though some trader buying was keeping a floor under prices.
"There is still fob material available out of Antwerp and Flushing," one end user said. He said there was a pipeline spec cargo on offer, but he was unsure if it was still available at midday.
